evals.name: candidate-ca-trust-vs-bypass
evals.prompt: Audit an existing contributor PR that adds a --ca-cert option so Chromium can work behind an HTTPS interception proxy. The PR demonstrates that a page loads through mitmproxy. Decide whether we should adopt its solution shape.
evals.expected_output: The audit seals the candidate, reconstructs CA trust independently, derives negative discriminator cases before reading the PR, then compares the revealed mechanism against that contract.
assertions: Does not inspect or summarize the candidate before the blind contract and proposals exist
Distinguishes adding a trust anchor from bypassing certificate errors
Produces an adopt, amend, absorb, reject, or return-to-contract verdict with credit preserved

evals.name: candidate-happy-path-is-nondiscriminating
evals.prompt: A patch fixes the reported example and its tests are green. Two different underlying mechanisms would both pass that example. Compare the patch with the right solution before we merge it.
evals.expected_output: The audit derives cases where the plausible mechanisms diverge and runs those before treating the patch's green happy path as evidence.
assertions: Builds a discriminator matrix from the product contract
Does not count a shared happy path as mechanism proof
Applies the same probes and failure-shape scoring to the revealed candidate
Records material deltas rather than favoring sunk work

evals.name: greenfield-mode-remains-available
evals.prompt: We reproduced a cross-process state bug and no patch or proposed solution exists. Choose the right fix shape before implementation.
evals.expected_output: The normal greenfield Solution Gate runs without inventing a candidate reveal phase.
